title: NHC wind speed probabilities in 2010-2025 were about 1.3 times too low for best-track and buoy 34-kt winds; the model's own wind geometry hides offsetting Pacific, hurricane and post-tropical errors
abstract: We tested the NHC/CPHC tropical cyclone wind speed probabilities (WSP, 120-h cumulative, 34/50/64 kt) with a pre-registered, timestamped plan. We used all 8,683 archived 0.5-degree grids for 2010-2025, the HURDAT2 best tracks of 603 Atlantic and eastern/central Pacific storms (18.8 million point-cycles) and, as independent truth, winds at 83 NDBC buoys. The frequency bias B is observed events divided by the sum of probabilities; intervals are 95 % storm bootstrap. With the pre-registered truth (full best-track quadrant sectors) the probabilities were too low: B = 1.31 [1.22, 1.40], 1.44 and 1.28 for 34, 50 and 64 kt. This did not hold with radii x 0.8 (B 1.02 at 34 kt). The WSP model uses 0.85 x interpolated radii. With that geometry (post hoc) the totals were calibrated (B 1.02, 1.13, 1.00), but through offsetting errors: eastern Pacific 0.75 vs Atlantic 1.15; storms below 64 kt 0.89 vs hurricanes 1.15 (the pre-registered weak-over-hurricane prediction failed in the reverse direction); Atlantic cycles with post-tropical stages 1.23 vs 0.95 for purely tropical ones. Because the sum of probabilities is the expected swath size of one Monte Carlo realization, B measures size errors. Per-cycle swath ratios followed official intensity errors (Spearman -0.21 to -0.40), not track errors. The eastern Pacific excess stayed at good intensity forecasts, so it is a wind-radius size excess. At buoys (98,901 buoy-cycles, 538 storms), measured 34-kt winds gave B = 1.33 [1.17, 1.49] (1.11-1.55 with the wind conversion); the full-sector truth matched buoy event counts (ratio 1.04) and the model geometry under-counted them (0.76). Limitations: best-track radii are analyses; the geometry choice is as large as the error; the model-geometry truths and the buoy test are post hoc; buoys do not decide at 50/64 kt.

Blue: pre-registered full-sector best-track truth; orange: WSP model geometry (0.85 x interpolated radii); green: same, tropical stages only. Bars: 95 % storm bootstrap; grey band 0.9-1.1.
